reader.name: Reader
reader.job: Reads each 10-K's income statement and cash-flow statement and returns revenue, cost of revenue (or its cost lines), operating income and capex for every year shown, each pointing at the cell it came from.
decides: Which row of the statement is each field
Which lines are a cost of revenue when there is no total line
The period of each column, and the unit to apply
checked_by: Every citation must resolve to the exact cell in the parsed table, or the answer is rejected and asked again once
Chrome re-reads every cited cell on the rendered 10-K
16 rules, the SEC's XBRL answer key, and a fault test of planted mistakes

ai_reader.name: AI spend reader
ai_reader.job: Reads the MD&A passages of each 10-K that mention AI next to capital or operating spending and returns every statement of how much goes to AI: a dollar amount, a share, or words only, each a verbatim quote.
decides: Whether a sentence states an amount, a share, or only words
Whether the figure is the AI part or the company's total with AI as a driver
Which fiscal year a sentence speaks to, and whether it is the reported year or an outlook
checked_by: Every quote must be a verbatim sentence of the passage it cites, or the answer is rejected and asked again once
An AI amount above the company's own capex for that year is a warning

notes_reader.name: Notes reader
notes_reader.job: Reads each 10-K's segment, property-and-equipment, lease and commitments tables and returns capex and revenue per segment, PP&E by category, finance lease liabilities and purchase commitments, each pointing at the cell it came from.
decides: Which note table holds each fact
What each segment or category is called, verbatim
Whether a column is a fiscal year or a year-end balance
checked_by: Every citation must resolve to the exact cell in the parsed table, or the answer is rejected and asked again once
The filing's own XBRL instance, where the fact is tagged with a segment or category member
